question: Which bond has highest duration (most price sensitivity)?
before: Duration increases with longer maturity and decreases with higher coupons. 10-year 2% coupon has longest maturity and lowest coupon -- virtually all value from distant principal repayment. Highest duration.
after:
Concept: Duration measures the weighted average time to receive a bond's cash flows, expressed in years. It is the primary metric for price sensitivity to interest rate changes. A bond with higher duration experiences larger percentage price moves for a given change in yield.

Step-by-step:

Duration depends on two competing factors: (1) maturity length — longer maturities increase duration, and (2) coupon rate — higher coupons decrease duration by returning cash to investors sooner. To find the highest duration, identify the bond with the longest maturity combined with the lowest coupon.

Compare each option:
A) 2-year, 8% coupon: Short maturity dominates; duration ≈ 1.9 years
B) 10-year, 8% coupon: Long maturity but high coupon pulls duration down; duration ≈ 7.2 years
C) 10-year, 2% coupon: Long maturity and low coupon; investor waits longest for cash return; duration ≈ 9.3 years
D) 2-year zero-coupon: No intermediate coupons, but short 2-year maturity limits duration; duration = 2.0 years

Result: Option C has the highest duration at approximately 9.3 years.

Why this is correct: The 10-year 2% coupon bond maximizes duration because it combines the longest maturity with the lowest coupon. The low coupon means investors receive very little cash until the final principal repayment in year 10, extending the weighted average time to receive cash flows and creating maximum price sensitivity to yield changes.

Why the others are wrong:
A) 2-year maturity is too short; even with 8% coupons providing some early cash return, the bond matures in just 2 years, yielding a duration well below the 10-year options.
B) While 10-year maturity is long, the 8% coupon returns significant cash to investors in early years, pulling down the weighted average life and reducing duration to around 7.2 years.
D) Although zero-coupon bonds have no intermediate coupons to shorten duration, the 2-year maturity is so short that duration equals exactly 2 years, far less than the 10-year alternatives.

Intuition: Equity analysts use duration to assess how much a bond fund or balance sheet asset will lose in value if the central bank raises rates. A bond with 9+ years of duration will drop roughly 9% in price for every 1% rate rise—far more than a short-maturity or high-coupon bond. This is why long-duration bonds are the most sensitive to monetary policy shifts and macro shocks.
